articleTitle: An Equivalent “Radiated Emission” Voltage Measurement Standard for Tem Cells
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The direct use of the voltages measured at the output of TEM and GTEM cells to evaluate the radiated emissions from electrical devices is considered. Most emission standards presently require that TEM cell measurements be correlated to OATS equivalent electric field values. A multipole model of the source as radiator is used to correlate between the two environments. In principle, however, it is possible to directly write a voltage standard for TEM cells which incorporates the multipole model correlation calculation. The result is a significant time savings since the calculation is not repeated for each individual device test. The paper explores the usefulness of such a direct standard through a set of measurements on two sample devices.

articleTitle: Sidelobe Suppression of Microstrip Patch Array with Nonuniform Excitation for Mobile Communication
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with fixed-beam planar arrays of microstrip rectangular patches that are envisaged for modern communication systems. In the contribution the general description of analysis and synthesis procedure for planar arrays and the passive Beam-Forming Networks (BFN) as well as the optimization procedure for array elements excitation are described. The array concept is based on (2×2) element subarray modular approach. The X-Band prototypes of (2×22) and (2×24) module arrays that utilize such approach, along with theoretical predictions, are presented. A good agreement has been obtained between the theoretical predictions and the measured results of the small array of linearly polarized rectangular patches with tapered amplitude (Taylor's distribution) and equiphase excitation. The theoretically predicted sidelobe level was kept below -25 dB (whereas-uniform excitation gives only -13 dB SLR).

articleTitle: Transient Electromagnetic Field Coupling to Multiconductor Cables
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The subject of this paper consists in the study of coupling between multiconductor cables (crosstalk) and coupling between these cables with an external electromagnetic field. We show the effects of electromagnetic pulses (EMP) on multiconductor line, suspended over a reference conductor (ground), in homogeneous or inhomogeneous medium. In the quasi-TEM assumption, we derive new matrix expressions of the terminated currents. The cables can be excited by generators of arbitrary waveforms and terminated by arbitrary impedances. The conductors can have finite conductivity. Time domain experimental and numerical results show how the perturbations can be reduced. Numerical results related to short lines, shielded cables illuminated by an electromagnetic field are presented.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Number of Natural Resonances Contained in the Radar Target Response Using E-Pulse Technique
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A technique to estimate the number of natural resonances of the radar-target response, based on the E-pulse scheme, is considered. This number is obtained by an iterative minimization procedure between the measured and the reconstructed response. Numerical results using the impulse response of a thin cylinder and a sphere, show that the technique is very insensitive to the presence of additive random noise which contaminates the radar-target response. Furthermore, by this procedure, an optimum E-pulse waveform and an optimum set of natural resonances can also be obtained.

articleTitle: Currents and Voltages Induced on Multiconductor Transmission Line by a Lightning Stroke
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents an application of the transmission line theory to determine the coupling of the electromagnetic field radiated by a lightning stroke discharge to a multiconductors shielded telecommunication cable. First the external problem is analysed and a particular attention is paid to the resolution of the internal problem. Then some results of calculations are presented in order to highlight the common mode to differential mode conversion in the case of NEMP disturbing waveform. Finally predicted results will be compared to some measurements obtained during artificially lightning experiments conducted at St Privat d'Allier.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility in Power Supply Devices with Inverted Rectifiers
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Important consumers put increased requirements to the quality of electric power consumed. These requirements are met by power supply systems with static inverted rectifiers operating in the separate mode. The essence of this mode consists in the fact that the power is supplied from power network not directly but in two stages. At first, it is transmitted to a separate accumulator, and then is given to a load. The processes of power accumulation and transmission to the load are time-divided, the-rebi eliminating a direct connection between the load power network and consequently their mutual influence, i.e. electromagnetic compatibility through the power network is ensured.

articleTitle: Identification of Results of Tests with Various Noise Simulators
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The most effective way to identify the degree of noise immunity of microelectronic devices are tests with the help of noise simulators. Various companies produce pulsing noise simulators modelling interference of various shapes and with various time characteristics. In order to process a sizeable statistical information accumulated during tests with different noise simulators it is necessary to solve the problem of idenitification of results. The spectral method is used in the presentation for a strict mathematical justification of the equivalence of various pulses and packages of pulses in respect to the rectangular-shaped pulse.

articleTitle: The Formulas for Calculating Electromagnetic Influence of Power Lines on Telecommunication Lines
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the universal calculation formulas for the electromagnetic influence of power lines an telecommunication lines for the case of their complex proximity are derived in consideration of the different distances between them.

articleTitle: Coupling of External Voltages with two Parallel Underground Conductors
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, the influences of external voltages on two parallel underground conductors are analysed by means of equivalent underground transmission line equations presented previously by the author. Both infinite length and finite length are taken into account in the calculation of currents and potentials along the conductors.

articleTitle: A Coaxial Peaking Circuit for the EMP-Simulation
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Peaking circuits are used to generate high-voltage pulses with rise times in the range of a few ns. The paper describes the numerical simulation of peaking circuits and experimental studies on test arrangements. The breakdown of the spark gap and the operation of the peaking circuit are calculated. The results are compared with experimental investigations.

articleTitle: On the Thunderstorm Overvoltages in a Coaxial Cables
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is shown that the main cause of the overvoltages in a coaxial cable line induced by a lightning discharge is a current and voltage wave CCWD in the cable shield and conductor appearing due to flowing away of charges attracted by the thundercloud electrostatic field. A mathematical models of the thunderstorm overvoltages in the coaxial cable taking into account the CVW phenomenon and time dependence of the lightning current also applicable in the permafrost region are suggested. A system of four algebraic relations between the coaxial cable distributed parameters generalizing the known "undistorted signal transmission" condition is found.

articleTitle: High-Speed Noise-Resistant Modem
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: At present moment high-speed data transmission systems usually are based on different types of quadrature-amplitude modulation and work only well signal to noise ratio is greater than 5-10. When narrow and wide bandwidth noise is present this ratio must be even greater. Demand to increase noise-immunity is high for airborn radioequipment because frequently a multitude of different radio systems work on one vehicle simultaneously. We offer modem designed for work in complex EM environment with data transmission rate of few hundred Mbps.

articleTitle: Notes from the Program Chairman
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This is the ninth time I am chairman of the Program Committee of this symposium (1976-1992). Moreover I was program chairman or vice-president of the Swiss EMC Symposium since 1975. As a member of the IEEE Society on EMC, I received all their recent Symposium Proceedings, and I was also a participant in several francophone EMC Symposia. Already in earlier Symposia I drew attention to the links between our Symposium and URSI, CISPR and CCIR. At this Symposium we have official sponsorship of URSI, and its Commissions E and F, resp. Electromagnetic Noise and Interference, and Wave Propagation and Remote Sensing. It is obvious analogous links should exist with URSI Commission H: Waves in Plasma (see papers on pages 566-558), and URSI Commission K: Biological Effects of EM Fields (see the topic Biological Effects of EM Radiation).

articleTitle: EMC Measurement Standards, Calibrations and Traceability
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A brief outline is given of the UK National Measurement System and the means of providing traceability in the UK. The role of NAMAS in providing accreditation services and working with our European partners to establish the mutual recognition of member states calibration and testing facilities is described briefly. The calibration services provided by NPL most relevant to EMC activities are also presented.

articleTitle: Estimation of EMC Conditions Eliminating the Intermodulation Interference in Land Mobile Cellular Radio Systems
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The EMC conditions of land mobile cellular radio systems are defined which eliminate the intermodulation interference in the reception channels of base stations. The dependence of probability of the interference absence on the three-signal selectivity of receivers is obtained. The graphical material is presented which allows to estimate efficiently the conditions of EMC provision in some practical cases.

articleTitle: Radio-Electronic Equipment EMC Ensured by Spatial-Temporal Processing of Signals
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problems of radio electronic equipment EMC with multielement arrays (A) are presented in this paper. The algorithms for determination of the optimum vector of weighting coefficients of A are synthesized, the vector defining the amplitude-phase distribution of currents on the aperture of antenna for the satisfaction of EMC criterion in various types of electromagnetic environment. To ensure REE EMC with A the systolic calculator consisting of two processor elements is synthesized.

articleTitle: EM Environment Analysis of Broadcasting Network in VHF/UHF Band Based on Test Points Concept
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a method of electromagnetic environment description of broadcasting network in VHF/UHF band. This approach is based on test points concept. The concept was practically checked for TV network. The test point database which represents spatial and spectral distribution of signals on the area under study is described. The presented approach proved to be useful in analysing of TV network and seems to be appropriate in advanced studies of services operated in VHF/UHF band. The paper discusses the development work, the current operation, and assess the advantages which have resulted.

articleTitle: Amateur Radio Service and EMC
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radioamateurs were pioneers of progress in radiocommunication from the very beginning. It were amateurs who had proved that shortwaves were useful for distant communication with low transmitter power. Radioamateurs have been involved in almost all the discoveries and in solving of important problems in electronics and radiocommunication as well as in their development. Radioamateurs were also ones of the first users of the electromagnetic spectrum who have been faced with problems of electromagnetic compatibility /EMC/. This paper has the aim to indicate on the main problems of EMC in the Amateur Radio Service /ARS/. Conclusions, of course, pertain also to other radio services.

articleTitle: Probes for EMP Measurement. Methods of Pulse Shape Reconstruction
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Two methods of reconstructing the real shape of the EMP are presented and compared. The methods involve deconvolution in the frequency domain and deconvolution in the time domain. Measurements were carried out, single-loaded loops, double-loaded loops, or high-voltage dividers.

articleTitle: Direction Finding of Exit Points of Whistlers and Causative Atmospherics at Low and Equatorial Latitudes
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to locate the exit points of whistlers and their causative atmospherics at very low and equatorial latitudes. The propagation mechanism of low and equatorial latitude whistlers and causative atmospherics is investigated on basis of spaced direction finding measurements in South China. It is found that the propagation mechanism of whistlers is satisfactory interpreted in terms of field-aligned propagation and causative atmospherics of whistlers are widely distributed in a range from 500km to 2,000km from the conjugate point of the ionospheric exit region. In this experimental fact, we may imply that stronger atmospherics can be trapped by a magnetospheric path even if they are located at a great distance from the entrance region. On the basis of these finding it is suggested that the field-aligned duct formation is more importance in the variation of whistler occurrence rate than the atmospherics activity at low and equatorial latitudes.

articleTitle: EMC in Power Switches
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes that main R.F. noises induced on power supply lines when switch is turned on/off are damped oscillation waveforms, clarifies their generation mechanism from the relationship between the resonance points existing on frequency-impedance characteristics measured about power supply lines and the “S” defined there and by applying the theory of resonance circuits made up of lumped constant L-C-R to the distributed constant circuits (that is, power supply lines), and insists that their suppression technique is to get rid of resonance points.

articleTitle: The Capture Effect in Localizer Receivers for Instrument Landing Systems
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This work reports on the capture effect in localizer receivers in order to assess the performance degradation of a two frequency null reference instrument landing system when the clearance signal is reflected back into the glide path. Calculations and a simulation test set up for airbom receivers have resulted in determining the effect of reflections from large buildings, and also the effect of other co-channel interferences on the course deviation indicator. Maximum limits are presented for retaining the runway category.

articleTitle: A Transmission Line Device for EMI Susceptibility Measurements with Enhanced Field Uniformity
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The subject of this paper is the analysis of a device for EMI measurements; the structure is similar to a TEM cell, with an inner wire array rather than a conducting septum. The transmission line is terminated in a resistor array at low frequencies, in anechoic material at higher frequencies. The device is referred to as wire TEM (WTEM) cell and is designed specifically to provide a high field uniformity in the test region. The performance of the WTEM cell is compared with that of TEM striplines. An enlarged quasistatic frequency band is available in the WTEM cell; moreover the coupling of the device under test with the structure is expected to be lower. The performance of the device as a standard EM fields generator has been predicted by a theoretical quasi-static analysis and estimated by measurements over a wide frequency band.

articleTitle: Apparatus and Software for Investigation of Radioelectronic Systems Stability to the Influence of Pulsed Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of experimental investigation of many EMC aspects obtained in the time domain on the base of pulse excitations are considered to be more informative than that obtained during the test by the harmonic signals. The experimental rigs, generating pulsed electromagnetic fields, data measuring complex and software developed and used at the test laboratories of the Kharkov Polytechnical Institute, realizing the advantages of the pulse excitation method, have been described. The technique for carrying out the experimental investigations which allows to construct mathematical model of nonlinear dynamic process of interaction of a definite element in radioelectronic system with electromagnetic field has been presented. The model allows to predict the behavior of the tested element in other electromagnetic fields.

articleTitle: Analysis of Specifications of Internation Standard IEC-801
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the actual problems of electromagnetic compatibility (HMC)of microelectronic devices is the adequacy of tests for their noise immunity by modelling pulsing interference. The parameters of model interference in the standard IEC-801 are specified in the time domain, the analysis of the standard specifications in the frequency domain present specific interest. The presentation uses mathematical methods of spectral analysis of the fourth part of the IEC-801 standard in its frequency domain. It is demonstrated that this part of the standard has serious shortcomings causing second order errors during compatibility tests. Ways are outlined to change the specifications of the fourth part to improve significantly the adequacy of tests.

articleTitle: EMC/EMI Standards, Measurements and Calibration Activities at Nist
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper discusses the EMC/EMI research activities at the National Institute of Standards and Technology. These activities are divided into four major categories: standard electromagnetic field generation, sensor technology, device/system emissions, and device/system immunity.

articleTitle: A Propagation Measurement Retrieval System
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Propagation Measurement Retrieval System (PMRS) contains a large number of measured propagation loss values with frequencies from 20 MHz to about 10000 MHz, antenna heights from 1 m to about 2400 m, for line- of-sight and beyond line-of-sight paths over rough terrain. These data currently reside in a computer system that was specifically designed to utilize the data with propagation analysis and statistical models to present the data in various formats. Most of the data in the PMRS has been submitted for inclusion in the CCIR Study Group 5 Data Bank.

articleTitle: Investigation of Electromagnetic Environment Produced by the Lightning Discharge "Cloud-Earth"
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The lightning discharges are considered to be the most widely spread source of electromagnetic interference. The electromagnetic environment produced by the lightning discharge destabilizes normal functioning of radioelectronic, electronic and electrotechnical equipment leading even to its failure. The determination of lightning electromagnetic environment (LEME) is considered to be one of the main steps in providing electromagnetic compatibility and in increasing stability of the equipment. The work is concerned with the investigation of formation of electromagnetic environment produced by the lightning discharge "cloud-earth" taking into consideration most of the factors, existing in reality. The lightning electromagnetic situation being formed both above and below the ground surface has been analyzed, and the amplitude-time characteristics of lightning electromagnetic pulse (LEMP) have been determined.

articleTitle: Direction Finding of Magnetospheric VLF/ELF Emissions and Their Generation and Propagation Mechanisms
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to review our recent studies on the generation and propagation mediamisms of magnetospheric VLF/ELF emissions based on the direction finding(DF) measurements on board spacecrafts in order to demonstrate the potential use of the direction finding measurements in plasma wave studies. The waves treated in this paper are, (1) half-gyrofrequency VLF emissions, (2) ELF hiss in detached plasma regions of the magnetosphere, (3) plasmaspheric ELF hiss, (4) VLF/ELF chorus and (5) hiss-triggered chorus.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility Punta Carretas Sewerage Pumping Station
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radio communications reception plants require very strict conditions about electromagnetic fields present in the same premises. This study treats the control of that kind of radiation, as produced by a Pumping Station which is installed nearby radio reception plants.

articleTitle: Conditions of Quantitative Changes of Nucleic Acids in Tissues of Animals Exposed to EM Energy
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The quantity of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA; in cells of any species is constant and it could be changed with the change of cells population in a volume of tissue. The genetic information encoded in DNA is transcribed to messenger ribonucleic acid (mBNA) which through transfer RNA [tRNA] translates it into proteins. Under thermal effect with specific absorption rate [SAR] of 10.5 W/kg due to short term exposure in EM fields there was no change of DNA quantity in the submaxillary salivary gland (SSG) of rats. An increased quantity of SNA has been found in SSG of rats exposed to pulsing EM field of 9.5 GHz. There was no change of DNA and SNA quantity in the pituitary gland of rats subjected to repeated long term exposure to E field of 50 Hz at 50 V/m.

articleTitle: Probability Characteristics of EM Environment in Zone of Action of the Land Mobile Radio Service
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper the analytical method of determination of the probability distribution of the interferring signals E<inf>n</inf> level effecting the receiver input is considered. The E<inf>n</inf> level is presented as the composition of the following random values: the distance between a source and the interference receptor, height of receiving and transmitting antennas, transmitters power and the antenna gain factor. As an example the results of the interferring signals E<inf>n</inf> are given which affect the receiver input of the land mobile service in a large city environment.

articleTitle: Far Field and Radar Cross-Section Calculation Using TLM Method
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The calculation of the far-scattered field and radar cross-section (RCS) of three-dimensional conducting complex bodies using the transmission-line-matrix (TLM) method with the symmetrical condensed node is presented. The calculation is based on a direct near- to far-field transformation in the time domain. Examples of far-zone-scattering results for traditional objects are given to validate the technique.

articleTitle: EMC Improvement of a Double-Sided Printed-Circuit Board
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Crosstalk reduction ways in printed-circuit board (PCB) inter—connections are considered and corresponding experimental results are given. A principle of the circuit board construction on the base of double-sided PCB located over the metal plate combining functions of a back signal conductor, an electron components carrier and a heat conductor is developed. It is shown, that using of such a board made on the base of conventional double-sided PCB technologies can give possibilities to reduce and control crosstalk values of high density interconnections, to improve the cooling of electron components by means of the metal plate heat conductivity and to provide the necessary environmental protection and proper electromagnetic shielding for the whole functional electronic block package.

articleTitle: New Trends in Computer Support of Spectrum Management
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Life is a parallel process in a multitasking multi-user environment. Sharing the same transmission medium is a specific feature of radiocommunications. The dramatic increase in the complexity of the radiocommunications environment requires improved Spectrum Management techniques. The role of Spectrum Management in maintaining both inter-system and intra-system compatibility can not be overestimated. Effective and rational use of frequency spectrum is therefore a key factor to the future development of (radio)communications. The need for powerful computer support of Spectrum Management therefore becomes a necessity. Current development both in Spectrum Management concepts and computer technology make the idea of CASM (Computer Aided Spectrum Management) systems realistic. Some aspects of CASM implementation and techniques are discussed in this presentation.

articleTitle: A Study of the Communication Immunity of Programmable Controllers in Regard to Indirect Electrostatic Discharges
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper are described the results from a study of the communication immunity of programmable controllers in regard to indirect electrostatic discharges. The study of the indirect electrostatic discharges is accomplished by means of an imitator and a vertical coupling plane (VCP), complying with the requirements of IEC 801 - 2. The experiments are carried out for different values of the discharge voltage, respectively for contact and air discharges on a VCP.

articleTitle: The Results of Statistical Analysis on Seismogenic Emissions in Japan
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Since 1980, we have detected impulsive noise bursts of seismogenic emissions at 82 kHz, 1525 Hz and 36Hz by a multipoint detection network around Tokyo region and Izu peninsula. In the earlier times, this system has recorded EM signals prior to several earthquake events. And they have recorded volcanic eruptions on November 15 and 21, 1986 at Mt. Mihara on Ohshima Island, on July 12, 1989 in Itoh Bay in the Izu peninsula region, and since June in 1991 at Mt. Unzen on the Shimabara peninsula. To obtain a clear explanation of the source mechanisum of these emissions, we were progressing in the statistical analyzes of these emission characteristics using the data of 29 events over the last five years.

articleTitle: Rationales of ISM Radiation Limits
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The International Amateur Radio Union (IARU) Reg.1 started its activity on the field of EMC years ago. The last works have been devoted to amateur bands protection against interference caused by Industrial, Scientific, Medical and Domestic (ISM) applications of EM energy. Contrary to radiocommunication these services are insensitive to any external interference, but they are able to affect the communication in wide frequency range and far away of the radiation source. On the ground of wideband and selective EMI analyses new proposals of ISM radiation limits, addressed to IEC and CISPR, were formulated. The proposals are presented and discussed in the paper. IARU proposals are more restrictive than the others because of long time experience of the Amateur Radio in coexistence with nearby EMI sources. The IARU expresses its hope that the proposals would find understanding and support from any other communication service.

articleTitle: Requirements on An EMC Testing Laboratory
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The requirements for an EMC test laboratory derive from current and upcoming standards, eg EN, CISPR, VDE, FCC. Particular attention has to be paid to the shielding attenuation of an enclosure, the attenuation of reflections and the attenuation of the absorber lining. The Implemetation of a complete EMC test center is shown. Here the focus is on the complete layout of a test laboratory, the location and style of the anechoic chamber, shielded control room and unshielded adjoining areas. The vital interfacing of the test instrumentation is looked at.

articleTitle: Two Methods of Evaluation of VHF/UHF Antenna Systems Radiation Patterns Comparison of Results
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Antenna system radiation patterns determine broadcast coverage and area of interferences in relations to other services. Radiation patterns are input data for computer software used in broadcast networks planning. Such patterns can be obtained in different ways. Two main methods of radiation patterns measurements: calculation from measured excitation coefficient and measurement using helicopter, are compared in this paper. The main reasons of results differences are shown.

articleTitle: Selected Problems of EMF Standards
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents activities of the Technical University of Wroclaw in the field of electromagnetic field measurements. The basic problem here is generation of standard EMFs and the activities have been started here. Now, in permanent use, are standards of H-field in frequency range 0-30 MHz, E-field in range 0-1 GHz, TEM & transfer E-field standards for the same range and microwave standards up to 10 GHz. The standards made it possible to design a variety of EMF probes and sensors for frequency range 0-10 GHz and to perform immunity and radiation measurements of many devices and systems. In the paper are discussed some detailed problems in EMF standards, eg.: the role of harmonics in accuracy and directional antennas calibration. Conclusions regarding international standards harmony are drawn.

articleTitle: Activities of EMC Standardization in China
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Since 1980's, 23 National Standards on EMC have been issued in China. This paper introduces the harmony with international standards in formulation process of these National Standards, and introduces the activities of National Technical Committee of Standardization on Radio Interference (NTCSRI), which was set up for promoting the standardization work on EMC.

articleTitle: Introduction of Non-Uniform Transmission Line into the Electromagnetic Topology Formalism
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Coupling to uniform transmission lines is treated by writting the so called BLT equation and allows the treatment of complex networks. However non uniform transmission lines such as non parallel cables inside a bundle, crossing of conductors are found in many practical cases. We show that the BLT equation formalism remains a well suitable tool to solve this problem by only discretizing the non uniform part of the structure.

articleTitle: Versatile Diffraction Modelling Techniques for Microwave Interference Propagation Prediction
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The effectiveness of modern-day radio planning and spectrum engineering is increasingly dependent on diffraction modelling for the determination of interference levels, and in many cases the wanted signal as well. Key problems include diffraction calculations for arbitrary terrain paths, and for cases where man-made "clutter" plays a significant role. This paper offers a new approach to macroscopic- scale diffraction modelling which features improved accuracy, straightforward formulation and fast execution speeds.

articleTitle: Measurement of Transfer Impedance of Coaxial and Multiwire Shielded Cables : A Review of the Recent Developments
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The first part of this paper deals with the measurement techniques to determine the transfer impedance of coaxial cables. Since most of the recent works concern the high frequency range (above 300 MHz), this aspect is emphasized. The second part is devoted to the difficulties encountered to characterize the shielding effectiveness of multiwire shielded cables both for the common mode and for the differential mode.

articleTitle: Application of Microwave Filters for Solving EMC Problems
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Various kind of the construction of selective filters are discussed and usefulness of evanescent mode waveguide filters for EM problems are shown. This filters in a single algorithm are design on rectangular, round and sectorial cross section evanescent mode waveguides. Results of design of the multimode waveguide filters frequency selectivity with ferrite, ferrite-dielectric and dielectric resonator are presented. Experimental and calculation data are discussed.

articleTitle: High Accuracy Method of Locating Distant Lightnings by Means of Tweek Atmosphereics
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The propagation characteristics of tweek atmospherics (with small dispersion effect) have been analysed by a new method in which the observed tweek signal is mixed with its corresponding pseudo-sferic signal, and the resulting nearly-stationary signal is analyzed by a conventional spectral analysis. Then, the propagation distance and ionospheric height are estimated in such a way that the squares of the difference of the instantaneous frequencies of the observed and pseudo sferic signals are made minimum. The method is applied to the VLF/ELF data simultaneously observed at Moshiri, Sakushima and Kagoshima in order to demonstrate the effectiveness of the method, and the accuracy in determining the propagation distance and ionospheric height is discussed.

articleTitle: Ferrite Antenna for Receiving Pulse Disturbances
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The design of the ferrite antenna for receiving the pulse disturbances is considered. The antenna is composed of two flat cores, the active and the passive one. The active core is wrapped by one turn of the flat conductor which is transformed into the strip line. The antenna makes it possible to receive pulses with the duration of up to 0.5 ns with the low waveform distortion. The antenna may be useful to estimate the level of the fringe radiation and to solve the EMC problem for antennas with nonsinusoidal signals.

articleTitle: EMC Estimation of Millimeter-Wave Radar Systems Operating with Wideband Signals
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Mathematical model for EMC estimation of two radars operating in the 30 to 300 GHz range and using continuous signals of large time-bandwidth product (like phase-shift M-sequences ) is considered in the paper. Modeling algorithm, basic formulas and some results of computer-aided experiments are presented. Recomendations for utilization of the model are given too.

articleTitle: EMC - Analysis in the Radio Frequency Space
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the so defined "Radio Frequency Space" (RFS), on the basis of the final dimentional linear vector-functional spaces the EMC-analysis tasks are sets, pointing the resolving ways. The RFS of a transmitter and RFS of a receiver is considered, as well as a conjugation method for the useful signals. The interference signals and the protection ratios of the interested receivers are described. The generalized description of the impacts among a great number of transmitters and receivers is givan. On the basis of the so mentioned theoretical model the algorythm for computerized EMC-analysis is suggested, examining two generalized cases: the algorythm for EMC - analysis for frequency coordination and the algorythm for EMC - analysis for frequency planning of a cellular mobile system.

articleTitle: Preliminary Experiments of Laser-Induced Lightning
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Induction characteristics have been investigated of a long-gap discharge in which the CO<inf>2</inf> laser-produced plasma is used as an induction channel. A long discharge length of 8.5 m has been achieved by using a new type of focusing mirror with three different focal lengths. A stepped leader is observed in laser-induced discharge. The mechanism of laser-induced discharge is also discussed.

articleTitle: Radiowave Propagation Studies in the Cost Programme
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Three COST projects on radiowave propagation topics have been conducted during the 20 year existence of the European COST organisation, and a fourth is now planned to start. These projects have concentrated on terrestrial paths above 10 GHz, earth-space paths above 10 GHz, interference paths above 1 GHz, and now wideband paths and millimetre wavelengths. The paper outlines the objectives and achievements, and why COST proved a particularly appropriate forum.

articleTitle: The Organization of Complex Study of Ionospheric Processes Dynamics and EM Field in the 1HZ-10MHZ Frequency Range at the Russia PE Region
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The organization of complex study of EM field and ionospheric processes dynamics including the measurement of both continuous (1Hz-10kHz) and pulse (10kHz-10MHz) component of the EM noise, the investigation of the fundamental ionospheric characteristics variation and ionized plasma component's dynamics at heights of 50-350 km by use of ground-based methods of radiosounding (10kHz-15MHz), and sounding by navigational (NNSSA) and geostationary (ETS-2, "Ekran") satellites signals, at the Russia PE region is described. The technique of experimental results processing and possibilities and perspectives of complex approach are considered.

articleTitle: Structuring the Interior Fields of a Bounded Wave EMC/EMP Test Facility by Impedance Loading of Waveguide Walls
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This investigation deals with structuring the interior electromagnetic fields of a bounded wave test facility by impedance loading of the waveguide walls. The analysis is relevant to the design of electromagnetic environments which can be used to evaluate the response of large systems against a transient vertically polarized electromagnetic pulse. The space-time-two-dimensional fields in the test volume are computed using the exact eigenfunctions of the impedance-loaded waveguide, also taking into account the reflection between the launching system and testing regions.

articleTitle: The Calculation of Resonant Frequencies in the Large NBS Tem Cell
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we have calculated the resonant frequencies in the NBS TEM cell by two methods which are FD—TD and irregularly graded TLM method. In the calculative process by the FD—TD method, we develop a novel processing method for the magnetic wall boundary conditions, with which it is possible to treat only one eighth of the whole cell domain to calculate the resonant frequencies. We also get an opinion about determining the field values at the intersection lines of two boundary planes. As a result, a great deal of useful resonant frequency data that haven't been published before are listed here. In the TLM method, we irregularly grade the propagation space according to the nature of the TEM cell. The results show that the coarseness error has been reduced evidently. Finally, a comparison between the results of these two methods is carried out, which show good agreement with each other.

articleTitle: German Radio Amateurs Complain of Radiation from Telekom's TV Cable Network
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The coaxial broadband cable system of Telekom employs the frequency range 47 to 300 MHz, thus containing the channels of TV bands I and III as well as additional S-channels, which in the open air are occupied by different radio services. Interference reports from similar cable TV systems have appeared in the english radio amateur literature since 1981. But also the german cable network is not free from interference to terrestrial radio services. Radiation as well as susceptibility have increased considerably by an allowance to connect buildings with existing private cable systems, originally intended for the distribution of terrestrial TV programmes only, to the Telekom cable network. When test tranmissions started on S6, interference to the amateur radio service was expecially noticeable in those cities where the local amateur repeater output on 145.750 MHz was interfered by the cable television sound carrier now appearing on the same frequency. In total, radio amateurs passed more than 9000 interference reports to the Deutsche Bundespost. However, reaction of Telekom on these reports has been poor. In some areas channel S6 was switched off, but in most others, this channel was later occupied by a regular TV programme. Treatment of interference reports was also disappointing. Due to this situation, the Deutsche Amateur Radio Club (DARC) argues that BAPT and Telekom are obviously unable to clear the interference in the amateur exclusive band 144 to 146 MHz and demands to switch off channel S6. Telekom, on the other hand, is stating that it has to meet the requirements of millions of TV clients and must insist on the use of all available channels. Independently of the outcome of this conflict it becomes evident that true compatibility between a commercially operated coaxial cable system and terrestrial radio services is very difficult to achieve, especially if they operate in close proximity to the cable. Therefore, to avoid these problems, future telecommunications systems should make increased use of fiber cables.

articleTitle: Seismogenic Electromagnetic Emissions in the Upper Ionosphere: Experimental Evidence
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An anomalous increase in the intencity of low-frequency (0.1 - 16 kHz) radiowave emissions was detected using Intercosmos-19 data when the satellite was nearly over the epicentre of an earthquake zone. Ample statistical data are the basis for a determination of the probable spatial- temporal dimensions of the region of the upper ionosphere in justify which ELP-VLP emissions were detected. The reliability of the detected phenomenon is 0.8-0.9. The ionospheric regions with the low-frequency emissions observed by Intercosmos-19 have been found to be formations ('noise belts') extended along ±60° of geographic longitude and ±2° of geographic latitude. The spectral characteristics of ELP-VLP emissions near seismic areas are specified. The earthquake depth and location under a continent or under an ocean has an effect on the results of the satellite observations of earthquakes.

articleTitle: A Simple Method for Estimate the Boundary of the Nearfield of a Line Source
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The microwave harsh is increasingly arouse the attention of general public. In this short paper we formiate a simple Method to predict the boundary of the nearfield of a line source. Since the wave in nearfield can be regard as propagate in a Gauss tube, so we construct three curves based on hyperblae as 6 dB, 15 dB and 20 dB boundary of the nearfield. It fits the calculate results very well. Since the pattern of rectangular antenna is identical with linear one, so the results can also be used for aperture antenna.

articleTitle: EMI Problems on GRP Ships
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a brief review of EMI problems which take place on the GRP (glass- reinforced plastic) naval ships. The sources of interferences are described. EMI reduction technics are proposed.

articleTitle: Internal Bonding Topology for new Communication Equipment
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper discusses the design and testing requirements of an equipment installed according to different national standards and operating company practices. In recent years, harmonization of communication system standards and safety standards became an important element of the evolution and growth of the international trade. International standards, such as the CCITT document K27 [1], attempt to capture various standards used for grounding of communication systems. This has resulted in various workable bonding and grounding topologies for both communication systems and computer systems. Suppliers and users of communication equipment are making significant efforts to ensure the effectiveness of bonding and grounding in their installations. In addition to personnel protection and proper equipment performance, requirements for electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) and system robustness to surges of energy are being considered. Since the international standards are not specific enough in details, additional standards within a particular grounding topology are being written and implemented. In Europe, one of those new supplementary standards will be the ETSI /EE2 [3] that is built upon the widely used CCITT Mesh-BN (MeshBonding-Network) topology.

articleTitle: A New Analysis Method of Nonlinear Scattering for Solution EMC Problems
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new analytical method for the solving of the nonlinear scattering problems based on the application on nonlinear boundary condition is suggested. It allows to determine space-frequency field distribution without the elaboration of a equivalent nonlinear arbitrary shape scatterer scheme. A number of model problem solutions are considered as an example, which permit to come to new conclusions about the influence of cylindrical bodies with definite amount and location on electromagnetic environment for the case of beharmonic excitation.

articleTitle: H. F. Radio Noises as a Diagnostic Tool of Global Morfology of the Ionosphere
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic emission in the topside ionosphere have been investegated on board of Intercosmos-19, Cosmoc 1809, Intercosmos-24 "Active", Intercosmos-25 "Apeks" satellite in the period 1979-1992. The paper presents the global picture of H.F. radio noises in 0.1-10. MHz frequency range. One of the most interesting features of global distribution of the observed spectra appears as remarkable enhancement of spectral density over Europe and Asia. This broad band emission in whole range of frequency can give a answer about the condition of ionosphere. The data coming from the satellite on board radio spectrometer can be also used as a tool for monitoring of the position and movement of the main ionosphere trough.

articleTitle: Review of the Cost 210 Hydrometeor Scatter Model
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper reviews the Hydrometeor Scatter Interference Prediction procedure developed within the European COST Project 210. Prior to COST 210, there was very little data available against which such models could be tested, and one of the major achievements of that project was to organise a range of experiments to provide reliable statistics of rain scatter. A brief description of the data resulting from this international collaboration is given here, together with a summary of the comparisons between model predictions and measurements.

articleTitle: The Potential Distribution of Conductor with Respect to Earth Along Telecommunication Line Provided with Neutralizing Transformer
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the theoretical formula is derived for calculation of the potential of conductor with respect to earth along telecommunication line with neutralizing transformer. In addtion for the convenience of its use in engineering project, a simplified formula and the calculation formula of number of neutralizing transformer in configuration are presented. Beside,the problem concerning the optimum method of configuration of neutralizing transformer is analyzed.

articleTitle: Increase of Accuracy and Bandwidth of Electromagnetic Pulse Measuring Instruments
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To increase measurement accuracy of electromagnetic pulse (EMP) parameters there has been developed a standard electromagnetic pulse generator which has electric field strength of up to 100 kV/m and rise time of up to 10<sup>-8</sup> s.A high voltage tunable TEM-cell is used as a fieldforming system. Reproduction error of maximum field strength is within 1-3 per cent. On the basis of a transmission line wide-band generators and EMP probes have been manufactured. They enable to reproduce and measure EMP having rise time of up to 3.10<sup>-10</sup>s.

articleTitle: A Modern Microwave Interference Prediction Procedure for Spectrum Management Applications
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: New microwave interference prediction procedures are needed to allow more effective spectrum engineering and radio planning. This paper introduces an approach originated by a major European collaborative project. COST210. which has recently been enhanced for global application through activity in CCIR Study Group V. The new prediction approach overcomes many technical and procedural problems inherent in existing methods.

articleTitle: MM-Wave Field Effects Upon Optical Properties of Aminoacid Crystals
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Investigation of the mm-wave (MMW) or extremely high frequency (EHF) radiation effect upon optical properties of α-glycine and β-alanine aminoacids was carried out by infrared (IR) reflection spectroscopy. MMW irradiation frequency was tuned in the range of 37-300 GHz. Incident power density of radiation varied from 10 to 100 W/m<sup>2</sup>. Drastic changes in shape and band intensity in the 800-1600 cm<sup>-1</sup> range were detected under MMW radiation action. There emerged an optional fine structure, depending on IR and MMW radiation polarization. The deformational vibrations of NH<sup>+</sup><inf>3</inf> and COO<sup>-</sup> groups in aminoacids were more sensitive to MMW radiation. A resonance character of MMW influence was determined. More than 20 resonances for alanine and 10 resonances for glycine were observed. Halfwidth of MMW radiation effect defined after NH deformational vibration changes was about 60-80 MHz. Amplitude of changes of the IR band intensities approached +.80% starting from initial intensity. As it was shown by the measurements, specimens temperature control (accurate to 0,5 K) did not vary in the process of changes. Nevertheless, the temperature control experiments demonstrated that specimens heating up to 320 K resulted in the well-known temperature widening of IR bands distinctly different from MMW radiation effect. The data obtained may be regarded as non-trivial and to explain them it would be appropriate to recruit the ideas of non-linear dynamic processes being, moreover, of collective nature. In particular, the possibility of multiphoton excitations in EHF field does not seem to be groundless because in permanent or low-frequency electromagnetic field lifetime of vibrational-rotational states may increase by several orders comparatively to visible range. Therefore, MMW irradiation may result in distribution not only in rotational states, but it may also change molecular redistribution in vibrational states. The multiformity of multiatomic molecule vibrational levels, the presence of numerous possibilities of Fermi-resonance manifestation, and in solid state - of Fermi-Davydov resonance - these factors add greatly to the probability of resonance interaction between EHF field and quasicontinuous spectrum of rotational-vibrational state of alanine and glycine.

articleTitle: The Worst-Case Estimate of the Mutual Coupling Effect on the Driving-Point Impedances of Closely Spaced Transmitting Antennas
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Mutual coupling effects between closely spaced antennas result in the degradation of antenna performances with respect to the nominal antenna parameters determined for isolated antennas. In the paper, the exact formulas are derived for calculating the bound of the antenna impedance change due to the effect of the other antenna system.

articleTitle: Estimation of Electromagnetic Interference Emitted from Cables of Telecommunications Equipment
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An electric field is created around a telecommunications line by common-mode currents caused by oscillator clock signals, switching signals of a power supply, and digitally transmitted signals. This field can constitute a potential source of interference to radio reception. CISPR/SCG and CCITT/SGV have been investigating test methods and disturbance limits at telecommunications signal ports. This paper describes measurement results for the interference field radiated from a telecommunications line and estimates the conversion from a signal's differential-mode voltage to a common-mode voltage, to validate the draft disturbance limits at telecommunications signal ports.

articleTitle: EMC in Cable Television Systems
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Paper deals with EMC of cable television systems. Sources of unwanted harmful radiation from active and passive components of cable television systems as well as the possibility of this radiation influence on the other telecommunications services work are discussed. Problems of cable television systems immunity to external fields are also presented. Permissible values of radiation from cable television systems and the immunity of these systems to external fields are proposed.

articleTitle: Biological Effects of EM Field on Randomly Selected Human Population Residing Permanently Close to the High Power, Long Wave Radio Transmitter, and Tradescantia Plant Model System in Situ
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The vast majority of people are exposed to much lower field strengths. There are several possible areas of biological interaction at low levels of exposure which our knowledge is limited. However many of the effects of exposures to nonionizing electromagnetic radiation, especially which result from acute exposure to extremely low frquency electric and magnetic fields, are well understood. This paper presents the examinations of a peripheral blood in human population which have lived in neighbourhood of the radio transmitter in Konstantynów, all through seventeen years. The compositions of a peripheral blood and some biochemical serum components or plasma, were examined. The significant changes of activity of hypophyseal-adrenal, hypophyseal-hyroid and dysfunction sodium - potassium pumps were revealed from of the level: corti sol, cholesterol, thyrotropic hormone, triiodothyronine, thyroxine, sodium, potassium, calcium, phosphorus, glucose. Also results of the studies performed in situ with Tradescantia plant model system are presented. Plants were exposed at several sites characterized by different frequencies (50 Hz, 225 kHz) and various electromagnetic field strength (2-375 V/m). These studies were realized in during of work, as well as without work of the radio transmitter. Statistically significant changes induced by this environment were observed. Effects of EMF on the somatic mutations rate, cell cycle and cell divisions in the Tradescantia Stamen Hair (TSH) System are presented.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Coupling into Rectangular Rack-and-Panel Connectors
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Measurement of the surface transfer impedance of both standard and EMI rack-and-panel connectors from 1 kHz to 100 MHz showed that the standard rack-and-panel connector provides essentially no electromagnetic shielding because it contains no positive mechanism for maintaining electrical contact between the plug and receptacle. Supplementary grounding devices reduce the transfer impedance to desirable levels for frequencies below a few tens of kHz. Electromagnetic shielding at high frequencies is minimal. Spring fingers around the periphery of the plus were very effective for maintaining electrical contact between the plug and receptacle and preventing electromagnetic coupling through the plug/receptacle interface. Control of the electromagnetic coupling through the plug/backshell interface was essential for good high frequency shielding performance. Gaskets installed in the plug/backshell interface were electromagnetically effective but cumbersome to install. At 100 MHz, the surface transfer impedance was dominated by the bonding impedance between the receptacle and the chassis. When spring fingers and a gasketted backshell were used, the transfer impedance of the rack-and-panel connector slowing increased from a fraction of a milliohm at low frequencies to several milliohms at high frequencies. This is about equivalent to the electromagnetic shielding expected of a quality circular connector and a good backshell.

articleTitle: Nonstationary Skin-Effect in the Wires of High Voltage Aerial Line and Deformation of Pulse Bave of Lighting Current
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The technique of analytical calculation of wave processes in the precorona regime in suspended above the ground nonmagnetic solid and tubular cylindric wires of two-wire homogeneous aerial line influenced by the pulse wave of lightning current induced by the principle discharge has been developed. It allows to determine the influence of nonstationary skin-effect and caused by it heat generation in circular wires of arbitrary thickness as well as geometrical and electrophysical parameters of aerial line for distortion and damping of the current running wave of lihgtning origin. It is shown, that for the long ranges (more than 1000m) of pulse wave of lightning current with the duration of 2/50 mcsec the pulse heat losses of energy in massive wires cause the considerable smoothihg of wave front and damping of current wave amplitude. In case of nonmassive wires there is no deformation of pulse wave front of lightning current due to joule losses in wires metal, one can observe only its damping. It is established, that intensity of wave processes damping in an aerial line increases with decrease in values of wires suspension above the ground, outer radius, wall thickness and conductivity of wires material. The obtained results allow to specify the solution of problems of electromagnetic compatibility and electric heat resistance of energy and electrotechnical power equipment, connected to the aerial line or located in the vicinity of it and influenced by the powerful pulse currents and electromagnetic interference of lightning origin.

articleTitle: Some Hypotheses to be Tested, Relating to Ion Migration Through a Membrane with Spatial Periodicity of its Properties
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: International and national standards for permissible human exposure to electromagnetic fields have been achieved. Further progress in refining these standards is slow, due partly to the lack of acknowledged mechanisms (other than thermal) for the interaction of EM fields and biotissue. This paper suggests a group of hypotheses, which (when formulated and tested, using the mathematics of wave-mechanics) might assist progress in this multi-disciplinary field. There are specific inter-disciplinary difficulties in the development of these hypotheses, and some of these difficulties are highlighted. The particular hypotheses which are proposed and developed are: (a) that ion tunnelling is described by the Schroedinger equation; (b) that, supported by the knowledge that the Schroedinger equation may readily be transformed into the form of a Hill equation, the resulting Hill equation can be fairly readily subjected to a stability analysis; and (c) that unstable solutions of (b) represent the loss of an ion trying to penetrate a barrier and stable solutions represent the transmission of an ion through the barrier. These hypotheses are to be tested, but the authors do not have the resources for further work in this direction. Other researchers are urged to pick up the challenge.

articleTitle: Calculation Methods of the Horizontal Component of Lightning Return Stroke Electric Fields
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Among the components of the electromagnetic field radiated by lightning, the horizontal electric field is the one more affected by a finite ground conductivity; in principle, its calculation is to be performed using expressions containing Sommerfeld integrals whose solutions require high computer time. The paper presents and discusses the validity limits of three different simplified methods (perfect conducting ground, wavetilt formula and Rubinstein approach) which allow to calculate the horizontal electric field component avoiding the solutions of Sommerfeld integrals. These simplified methods, within their validity limits, represent a powerful tool for power engineers when LEMP is used as input for "coupling” calculations in order to determine lightning-induced overvoltages on transmission lines.

articleTitle: Nervous and Humoral Mechanisms of Weak ChMF ELF Antistress Effect
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It was stated that changeable magnetic fields (ChMF) of 8 Hz frequency 5 mcTl induction bring about more effective adaptation of animals to limited mobility. In the realization of the ChMF modifying effect on hypokinetic stress development the central nervous system (CNS) and sympathetic adrenal system are of major importance. Still, the ChMF influence on rats hypomobility resulted in decreasing the nervous system reactivity and led to the inhibitory processes intensification within the centers, hupothalamus functional activity modification, significant adrenaline increase in urine and in erythrocytes and synchronization of the biological rhythms activity of sympathetic adrenal system.

articleTitle: Topics on Recent EMC Development in Japan
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Test methods of radio interference and immunity for information technology equipment(ITE) have been developed in Japan to resolve the problems arising from electromagnetic disturbances. The measurement methods and countermeasures are also being developed to confirm electromagnetic compatibility(EMC) characteristics. This paper reviews the major technical achievements in Japan which play an important role in EMC area, such as recent progresses in anechoic chambers, countermeasures for telecommunications equipment, and antennas which use optical technology.

articleTitle: Multicriteria Design of Power Factor Correction Devices as the Mean to Improve the EMC in the Network with Nonlinear Loads
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the sources of poor EMC within the power supply network are the nonlinear loads which are drawing the distorted current from the power source what as consequence results in the voltage wave distortion in substations jointly supplied from the common distribution point. These distortions can be amplified by resonance phenomena between the network inductances and capacitances of power factor correction devices occurring for higher harmonics of power system frequency. Nowadays when many modern receivers have its power consumption controlled by means of thyristors the voltage wave distortion is often encountered. The compensating capacitor bank being optimized regarding the economy calculated for the first harmonic of voltage and current can contribute to the worsening of the electric energy quality supplied from the network. In such cases the new criteria for the capacitor bank design, taking into account the voltage distortion in the nodes, have to be also considered. It is rather difficult to put them into one general cost equation. Voltage distortion can badly influence the operation of various sensitive receivers however this phenomenon can be hardly counted as cost because even its technical meaning depends on receiver type. To keep the voltage distortion on the safe level the limit values on individual harmonics or on factors characterizing the overall voltage distortion are set and considered as standard or recommended levels. It seems obvious that the distortion on the level close to the limit value is approximately as costly as a little bit higher value exceeding the set limit but only the first situation is permissible. From the other side voltage distortion increase the overall active power losses in the supply network what can be taken into account in form of separate objective function. The second problem which one encounters is the fact that usually the harmful voltage distortion values are different for various nodes in the considered supply system [1,2,3]. It can be seen from limit standard values which decrease with the voltage increase. The distribution of sensitive receivers should be also taken into account in the manner to introduces more restricted values for distortion limits in the nodes where the risk of damage is greater. Thus the individual consideration on voltage distortion in network nodes is recommended.

articleTitle: Crest Factor Sensor for Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a new instrument suitable to measure the Crest Factor of an Electromagnetic (EM) field having unknown polarization and direction of propagation. The instrument is based upon the simultaneous detection in isotropic mode of both the peak value and the RMS value of the EM field and then the evaluation of the ratio of these two quantities. This instrument is particular useful for the EMC and Radiation Hazard activities because allows a more complete characterization of the EM field. A prototype and some experimental measurements of electric field are presented.

articleTitle: International Activity on Prediction of Signal Levels Likely to Cause Co-Channel Interference
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The need for improved predictions of signal levels likely to cause interference in Europe produced a six-year COST study which has produced extensive new data and a recommended prediction procedure. Extensive studies have been conducted for clear-air conditions, for hydrometeor-scatter conditions and for site-shielding. This European work has been followed up in the worldwide forum of CCIR, with a very favourable outcome.

articleTitle: Changing Environments
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Each electric and electronic apparatus should have the ability to operate satisfactorily in the EMC environment for which it is designed, without causing interference to radiocommunication services or to other apparatus in its environment. To reach this goal, each apparatus must fulfil certain EMC requirements.

articleTitle: Describing and Testing the Immunity of Devices on a Statistical Base
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The immunity of electronic devices to electromagnetic disturbances has commonly been considered and tested in form of a deterministic quantity (see e.g. IEC 801 or DIN VDE 0843). From practical experience it is well known that accuracy and reproducibility of the test results are unsatisfyingly in many cases, especially when pulse-shaped test quantities are applicated. The reason is that the immunity factor S<inf>Fj</inf> of an equipment under test (EUT) to a definite test quantity z<inf>pj</inf>, which enters the EUT at a special port, is influenced by many random variables. The related problems will be diskussed.

articleTitle: Varistor-Composite Materials as Transient Protection Structures in Electronic Circuits
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electronic equipment and components that use semiconductor devices have a very low upset and damage threshold. Antennas are input ports for electromagnetic threats (lightning, EMP from nuclear weapons, etc.). Varistor-composite materials provide protection against them with their nonlinear behaviour and fast response time. In this communication, a numerical analysis of wire antennas loaded with varistor-composite materials is carried out. Selecting the characteristics of the material, the nonlinear load drains off currents of excessive electric-field strength. At operating voltages, the nonlinear element presents a higher impedance path and the interference is minimal.

articleTitle: Study of Two Channel Interference Canceler for Microwaye Communications Systems
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: 1. The report presents the results of theoretical and experimental studies of interference cancellation efficiency achieved in microwave links with angular modulation when the use is, made of two channel interference canceler.

articleTitle: Some Problems Concerning of Frequency Continuity and Evaluating Interference for HFBC Planning
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of HFBC planning are determined by different factors of physical, economic and political origin and therefore the planning is very complex process and results of it are difficult to foresee. Some especial features of planning conditioned by frequency continuity and evaluating of interferences in broadcasting channels are discussed in this paper. The HFBC planning is usually realized for each hour as the number of requirements and ionospheric propagation may vary from hour to hour. The system for personal computer to select suitable broadcasting frequencies taking into account broadcasting stations data is described. Data base dBASE III Plus is used for data processing. The experience gained by the IFRB on designing similar systems was used.

articleTitle: Prediction of Radiation from a Metallic Box with Apertures
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of the radiated emission from apertures in metallic enclosures has been theoretically and experimentally investigated. In particular the evaluation of the electric field on the aperture is helpful during the design stage of an electronic equipment, shielded by a metallic box, to predict its radiated emission. A rigorous approach, based on the equivalence principle, has been used; it leads to an integral equation solved by the Method of Moments. Numerical simulation is in good agreement with experimental results.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Noise Spectra of Corona Discharge at Point-to-Plane Electrodes in Air
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic(EM) noise spectra were measured with a set of rod antenna and a spectrum analyzer in UHF and VHF bands. The EM noise of a corona discharge with stationary electrodes which are employed in plasma reactors for NOx treatment were compared to that of a complex discharge with rotating electrode which is utilized in an ignition system of a vehicle.

articleTitle: Peformance of a Quasi-Coherent Binary PSK Demodulator
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A quasi-coherent binary PSK demodulator suitable for systems with burst signal transmission in the presence of cochannel interference is studied analitically. This demodulator employs a locally generated reference carrier. The reference carrier is generated by a polyphase oscillator. It is shown that the proposed quasi-coherent demodulator performance is nearly identical to that of binary DCPSK demodulator with perfect phase reference.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Pulse Simulator
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An electromagnetic impulse simulator composed of parallel-plate type antenna, EMP generator, HV power supply and measuring /auxiliary equipment has been described. Parameters and characteristics of the simulator as well as capabilities and methods used for simulating the lightning electromagnetic threats (LEMP) have been presented.

articleTitle: Desegmentation Method of Analysis of Dual-Frequency Operated Layered Microstrip Array
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A microstrip patch antenna array for use with a GPS receiver has been developed. The main purpose of this paper is to present microstrip stacked rectangular-ring patches with low cross polarization over the extremely wide beamwidth (close to hemisphere). The desegmentation technique (multiport network modeling coupled with cavity model) approach providing a detailed equivalent network representation of microstrip patches, mutual coupling among them, and for probe feed of an array has been used. It is a convenient framework for CAD of microstrip patch antennas and arrays. Antenna operates for two-bands ( 1227 and 1575 MHz) of GPS signals with an axial ratio less than 3 dB over an angle 140° and VSWR less than 1.5 over 20 MHz bandwith centered around each frequency.

articleTitle: Tem Cells Modelling Using TLM Method
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
