abstract: In this work the TEM cells were modelled using both two- and three-dimensional TLM methods. Cutoff and resonant frequencies were calculated as well as the electromagnetic field distribution in the work volumes. The influence of putting an object into the cell was investigated. Results were verified experimentally using HP 8752A Network Analyzer.

articleTitle: Method of Calculation of the Protection Distance Between Man-Made Interference Sources and Radio Receiving Objects
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper the method is proposed for calculation of the protection distance between sources of the man-made interference and radio receiving objects. The protection distance is determined from a condition of obtaining of the specified reception quality with certain reliability. Expressions for calculation of the protection distance under the interferring influence by the fundamental and non-fundamental reception channels are obtained as well as under the influence of interference from some sources.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Noise Connected with Seismic Activity
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Now it's clear that earthquake is not a spontaneous event, but a process, which is being prepared for much or less time and which manifests itself in different physical phenomena. Analysis of the whole variaty of information leads to the construction of the earthquake model. It is understood as description of processes preceding, accompaning and following the main shock. Many different earthquake models are known today and their number is growing because of the appearance new ones and modification of old. Models are very diverse in details. However they have more or less common features because they describe the same process /1/ (see Fig.1).

articleTitle: Intermodulation Immunity of FM Receivers
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The intermodulation phenomenon in the FM receivers limits the number of radiostations which may work simultaneously on the same territory without loss of their reception quality. The problem is particularly important in the big cities where the demand for stations in the VHF band is great. Paper presents the results of FM receiver input intermodulation immunity investigations and compares them with EN 55020 requirements. Some advices for radiostation network planners are given.

articleTitle: Terrestrial VLF Noise in the Region of Cape Shmidt During a Solar Eclipse on 22 July 1990
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: During a solar eclipse on July 22, 1990, in the region of Cape Shmidt (181°E, 69°N; measurements of discrete natural emission intensity at frequencies of 1.6 kHz, 4.2 kHz, 5.6 kHz and in an ELE range (5-200 Hz) were carried out. All pulses exceeding a fixed threshold, irrespective of their form and duration, with a discrete signal meter were registered. At all these frequencies during the eclipse a hurst of the discrete emission intensity reaching typical nighttime values was detected. The most probable reason of the discovered effect lies in a substantial growing of the level of ground-based VLF noise of a magnetospheric origin.

articleTitle: The Measurement of Field Strength in a Screened Enclosure
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes how selectively placed RAM can be used to greatly reduce the Q value of the natural resonances of unlined screened rooms. This provides a stable and reproducible measuring environment where emission measurements agree with those obtained on an open-site range to within 5 dB over the frequency range 30 to 200 MHz. The effectiveness of the RAM damping has been demonstrated in two rooms of different sizes and aspect ratios.

articleTitle: Investigation on Calibration Techniques of a Standard Dipole Using Transmission-Line Method and Standard Field Method
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the facilities and an investigation carried out on test procedures for the calibrations of horizontally polarized radio frequency electric dipole at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Boulder, Colorado, USA.

articleTitle: Coupling-Decoupling Networks for Surge Immunity Tests: An Example of Design
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Presented are two coupling-decoupling networks for testing the immunity of electronic devices to both oscillatory and pulse type surge waves. In the networks proposed, the device under test can be fed with normal current up to 16 A. The admissible pulse amplitude amounts to 6 kV. The coupling-decoupling networks meet the European Standards IEC-801 and IEC-255, as well as the Polish Standard PN-86/E-06600.

articleTitle: Developing Carrier-to-Interference Performance Objectives at the RF Spectrum in the Common-Carrier Band
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the basic concept for developing objectives for the fixed tolerance ratio (C/I) of desired carrier signal (C) to undesired interference signal (I) for four different types of communications systems. It then outlines procedures for developing C/I objectives by using currently available software, and shows how these procedures can be integrated into a single software package.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiviness of CATV System
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This work concentrates on the screening effectiviness of a distribution system, the subpart of a community aerial system. In Finland the method for the measurement of leakage radiation has been designed, and it is now under development in IEC and GENELEC Commitees. In this report we determine the worst case limits for protection of the various land mobile services from interference from a distribution system. In conclusion, we present our latest measurement results and discuss future aspects.

articleTitle: Determination of Lightning Transients in Wires and Loops within the Buildings
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A particularly hazardous to electronic equipment is a direct lightning stroke to the building or its vicinity. This paper proposed a method for theoretical determination of currents and voltages induced by LEMP in simple arrangements of cables and big loops formed by power supply. signal wires and conducting elements in building. The cables were placed over a perfectly conductive plane inside the building and closed with the resistances modeling the inputs of electronic devices. In calculations the shapes of the first and succesive lightning currents in the channel are correctly described.

articleTitle: Match Conditions of Links of Radio Interference Passive Filters
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A technique of Radio Interference Passive Filters (RIPF) synthesis is presented. The proposed procedure of RIPF synthesis allows to provide the maximum attenuation frequency band at minimum number of RIPF links and at match of links frequency response which was obtained taking into account parasitic parameters and losses in components of RIPF. The strategy of filters synthesis is realized as the algorithm for computer-aided design of RIPF. The results of theoretical and experimental studies of RIPF frequency responses are presented.

articleTitle: Conditions of the ESD Research
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The conditions of the ESD from a surface of charged solid dielectric flat-parallel sample to a grounded spherical electrode were investigated. On the other side of the sample a grounded counter electrode was placed. An analytic formulae describing the distribution of the stationary electric field along the symmetry axis of the system and in particular on the surface of the discharging electrode were found. The measurements showed the influence of surface resistivity and half time decay of surface potential of the examined samples on the ESD initiation. The effect of the contact of the sample with the counter electrode was determined.

articleTitle: Models for the Effects of Electromagnetic Fields on the Occurrence of Cancer
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Two models have been developed that could explain how electromagnetic fields effect the occurrence cancer. In both models the electromagnetic fields act in a secondary way. In the first model stress due to electromagnetic fields enhances the cell division rate and in the second model, electromagnetic induced stress adversely affects the immune system. They use credible mechanisms, are consistent with observations and can be used to make predictions for future research efforts.

articleTitle: New Emission Measurement Methods for an Electrically Small Source: A Three Loop Method and a Tem Cell Method
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This short paper proposes a method for determining the radiation characteristics of an electrically small source. The source is located at the center of three orthogonal loop antennas, each terminated with identical loads at diametrically opposite points. The electrically small source is represented by equivalent electric and magnetic dipole moments, and these dipole moments can be determined from the appropriate combinations of the loop responses.

articleTitle: Development of EMC Standards for International Harmonization
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the development of Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) standards in the Republic of China (R.O.C.). The progress of electromagnetic interference (EMI) testing laboratories set up in R.O.C. and laboratory accreditation in EMC testing by the Chinese National Laboratory Accreditation (CNLA) are given. Present status of the Microwave Laboratory in the National Measurement Laboratory (NML), R.O.C., for providing international traceability to EMC standards is also described.

articleTitle: Limitation of Intermodulation Effects in the C.I.S.P.R. Interference Measuring Apparatus - Necessary Changes in the Publication 16
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The C.I.S.P.R. intermodulation test of radio interference measuring apparatus (Publication 16, Clause 4) should be changed. Results of the current version of the test are not unambiguous and shall not be used for valuation of intermodulation properties of measuring apparatus. In the paper necessary changes of the C.I.S.P.R. test conditions are discussed.

articleTitle: Thyristor-Based High Immunity Logic Microcircuits for Industrial Automation Systems
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The thyristor-based logic microcircuits in question simplify immunity arrangement for Industrial automation systems. The use of thyristors as active components, which are capable of storing the control signals up to the end of supply voltage period, enhance circuit immunity by logic nil, and probabilistic methods of signal processing by logic one. The methodology and results have been furnished of the microcircuits immunity analysis, the above analysis having been conducted with the use of statistic modelling via a digital computer.

articleTitle: A Technique for Optimizing Spectrum Usage in Microwave Radio Systems
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: With the sharp increase in the number of microwave radio stations, the need to determine proper coordination distances to avoid interference between stations has become critical. This paper describes a model for determining the coordination distance, using a “keyhole concept.” This model has been shown to be more efficient than the currently used technique. It also gives several calculations that show the variations of coordination distances at different antenna heights.

articleTitle: Diurnal Variations of Wide Band VLF - LF Atmospheric Radio Noise at Middle Latitudes in Winter
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Results are represented of statistical simulation of the formation proces of atmospheric noise(AN) spectral density (SD) in its diurnal variations; SD being determined by changes of earth - ionosphere waveguide(EIW) spatial and time characteristics and of the intensity of distant thunderstorms. The results are being compared to experimental data obtained in winter near the city of Gorky.

articleTitle: H.F. Emission Related to Electron Beam and Plasma Injection into the Ionosphere
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electron beams and plasma have been injected into the ionosphere for many years from the payload board for many purposes. The H.F. emission related to these beam-plasma systems displays structure, which is crucial if we intend to use the possibilities of application of the beam as the radiating antenna in space. This paper presents experimental results obtained during injection of electron beam into the ionosphere from the board of GRUZIYA-60-SPURT rocket and obtained during Li<sup>+</sup> plasma injection from the board of PLAZMA rocket.

articleTitle: On the Reflectionless Dielectric Medium Theory
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic wave transmission through a one-dimensional irregular medium with soliton permittivity (1) is theoretically studied. It is shown that For H — polarized waves, unlike E - polarized waves, the resonance frequencies are a function of the angle of incidence. A choice of the medium parameters which provide a minimal E — and H — polarized wave reflection is discussed. The effect of a dielectric absorption on a resonance wave transmission is investigated. The cut of effect of a continuous soliton distribution on the resonance transmission is analyzed.

articleTitle: Interference from EHV Transmission Lines at Frequencies Above 30 MHz
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Interference sources from transmission lines at frequencies above 30 MHz are considered. Interference investigations on operating lines in the frequency range of 30-1000 MHz were carried out. Values of the lateral interference attention factor and the factor of interference attenuation with frequency growth were obtained in the above range. Measurement results were evaluated in accordance with USSR standards. Methods for locating interference sources and correcting defects are given

articleTitle: Corona Noise of HVDC Transmission Line
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes on the following aspects of corona noise in the frequency range around 1 MHz generated by conductors of HVDC transmission line: 1) General performance of corona noise from HVDC line conductors and features of dc corona noise compared with ac corona noise 2) Outline of a theoretical basis on RI generation, propagation and a method of analyzing corona noise taking account of the conductor surface gradient in the presence of space charge 3) Prediction method of corona noise level in the vicinity of HVDC transmission lines and the application examples

articleTitle: To the Problem of Estimation of Current Probe Orientation Error
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The investigations of metrological characteristics of the current probe recommended by CISPR as radio interference measuring device has not been finished yet. In particular there is need to study the error originated from the uncertainty of its orientation relative to the current carrying conductor. It is obvious that the analysis of the origin of the current probe orientation error will contribute to the search of measures to be taken for this error possible elimination.

articleTitle: Satellite Broadcasting Planning Aspects in the Wake of the Warc-92
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: New technologies (digital transmission methods, satellite distribution systems, etc.) have facilitated the potential for a more efficient use of the frequency spectrum. The possibilities of applying these new developments in planning, using frequency bands allocated to satellite broadcasting services (digital sound and HDTV) at the WARC-92, are discussed.

articleTitle: Lightning Fault Expectancy for Optic Fibre Cables
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Buried optic fibre cables with incorporated metal parts as moisture barrier, central metal wire, copper wires or steel armouring can be destroyed by a lightning striking to the earth in the vicinity of the cable. To decide whether the lightning protection of these cables is economic or not, the knowledge of lightning fault amount is decisive. The paper deals with the problem, taking into account different construction modes of the optic cable with metal parts.

articleTitle: Selected Aspects of Standardization in the Field of EMC
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper focuses on standardization from an IEC Central Office perspective. It deals with two independent subjects: 1. Implementation of the IEC/CENELEC cooperation agreement. 2. Bilingualism and IEC work Both subjects are highly relevant to the efficiency of standards development.

articleTitle: Studying of Anti-Interference Matching-Filter for Automatic Block Signalling System
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To meet the demand of the fail-safe principle for signalling equipment on electrified railway, several relevant anti-interference matching filters have been designed that are used in several types of automatic block signalling systems affected often by electrified traction. Each of the filters has a great attenuation to interference but has no influence on the automactic block signalling.

articleTitle: Pi - 2 Pulsations Associated with Substorm Current Wedge
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Substorm associated Pi-2 magnetic pulsations are frequently detected by satellites at the synchronous orbit. The simultaneous observations of this category of pulsations recorded by GOES-5 and GOES-6 on 22 April, 1985 between 0500-0700 UT have been presented. During this interval of time GOES-6 was staying in pre-midnight sector and has recorded positive (eastward) variation in the magnetic field and GOES-5 was staying in post-midnight sector, and there fore, detected negative (westward) variations in the magnetic field. Our power spectral analysis shows that the pulsations recorded during the interval of 0540-0550 UT were associated with substorm current wedge and other two events took place when satellites were located 3way from this region.

articleTitle: Bonding Configurations for Telecommunications Installations
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) measures that are included in the new CCITT Recommendation K.27 concerning bonding configurations and earthing inside telecommunications buildings. It introduces the definitions and configurations of the Recommendation, and presents qualitative rationales for the EMC measures. It also introduces efforts in CCITT Study Group Five concerning bonding configurations and earthing at subscribers' premises.

articleTitle: Investigation of Interference in Underground Mining Communication Lines
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Interference on under ground mining communication lines is time dependent. Its variation contains determinate and random components. The paper concerns the random variation of the interference. Examples of interference on symmetrical wire lines were measured and recorded in a few Polish coal mines. Two interference signals were recorded : the transverse interference voltage Csymmetrical interference) and the interference voltage between the symmetrical line and the ground Casymmetrical interference). The recorded voltages were analysed by microcomputer. The results of the analysis gave some time and amplitude characteristics of the interference and the correlation between the symmetrical a asymmetrical interference.

articleTitle: Interference Reduction at Microwave Radio Terminals Using Site Shielding
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Site shielding is an interference reduction technique which utilises obstacles such as buildings, to shield a radio receiving terminal from an interfering signal. The paper summarises results based on extensive measurements obtained for line-of-sight radio paths at a frequency of 11.2 GHz using a number of buildings. The results obtained under COST 210 in conjunction with CCIR prediction models are presented.

articleTitle: Schumann Resonance Modes Influenced by the Eclipse of the Sun
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The latitudinal dependence of relative phase velocity <sup>C</sup>/v and attenuation rate L of the Earth-to-ionosphere cavity ULF field is considered in terms of its homogeneous model solution. The <sup>C</sup>/<inf>V</inf> and L variations during solar eclipse are estimated by two-step approximation of disturbed ionosphere. The calculated data of the absolute peak levels of three Schumann modes and their frequencies well agree with the cited experimental evidences of solar eclipse.

articleTitle: Basic Changes Required in National Spectrum Management
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Basic changes are required in National Spectrum Management to ensure flexible and effective use of the radio spectrum. The radio spectrum is crucial to communications and the national economy in all countries. Policies for managing the spectrum must ensure that the spectrum is used efficiently and fairly, while promoting innovation and serving users’ needs. Administrations need to make changes to the spectrum management structure, processes and spectrum allocations that will address new user requirements in a more "open," flexible and timely manner, and promote new spectrum efficient technologies. In addition, market based approaches and strategic planning techniques need to be applied to the assignment and allocation of the spectrum resource.

articleTitle: Lightning EMP Effects on Data Transmission Lines in HV Substations
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents calculation results of lightning-induced overvoltages on a typical transmission-data line in a HV substation.  The line consists of a horizontal part installed in a cable duct and a vertical section at one end. The contribution of the electromagnetic field coupling to the horizontal and vertical parts of the line is analyzed and discussed. The calculations are performed using a lightning return stroke current model previously introduced by the authors and the coupling model introduced by Agrawal et al., An equivalent circuit based on this model has been proposed and used for the specific configuration. It is shown that nearby indirect lightning strokes (3 km distance) may induce dangerous overvoltages on the data line. It is also shown that for the considered HV substation transmission line which horizontal part runs close to the very good conducting ground of the substation, the electromagnetic coupling with the vertical section is predominant with respect to the coupling with the horizontal pan.

articleTitle: The Effect of the Isolated Obstacle Upon Lightning Direction Finding System
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, the scattered field resulted from isolated obstacle is idealized as the field produced by an equivalent electric dipole, the effect of the scattered field upon lightning direction finding system is analyzed. The deviation of the determined lightning direction is evaluated. The evaluations coincide with our measurements in the Summer 1990.

articleTitle: Unintended Interference Effect on Characteristics of Data Packet Delivery Over Radio Channels
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The principles of estimation of unintended radio interference (RI) effect induced by radio-electronic equipment (RE) on characteristics of data packet delivery over radio channels are considered. Relationships have been obtained which specify probability-timing characteristics (PTC) of packet delivery at stable mode functioning of one class of telecommunication network (TN). Examples are given which show dependences of probability and mean time of data packet delivery on their arrival rate from subscribers, assumed conditions of RE electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) and intersystem RI parameters.

articleTitle: Testing of EM Energy in a Specified Volume of Space
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The human body may be designed by simplified geometrical volume: sphere-shaped head, column-shaped trunk and symmtrical extremities. The "coil model of man" could be made from many spiral loops with diameters adequate to different parts of the human body. Prototype of such a model has been made from copper-foil belt. With the use of prototype the selective and broadband electric signals have been monitored from electric and magnetic fields within quite large frequency range.

articleTitle: Efficiency of the Magnetic Field Therapy for Paroxysmal Schizophrenia Patients Depending on its Application Location
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The findings on the efficiency of the magnetic field therapy on schizophrenic patients are demonstrated in a report. The main attention is paid to Electromagnetic Field Influence (EFI), which has unspecific nature and affects blood flow and metabolic processes normalization occuring owing to blood flow changes which result in altering of the equilibrium between free oxidation and phosphorylation, leading to protein metabolism in patients with endogenous psychosis. An attempt to demonstrate right and left hemispheres unequivalent participation in psychopathological symptomatica genesis of schizophrenic patients, the ways of their synchronization and reducing resistance of patients under EFI was made in a report.

articleTitle: European Aspects of Spectrum Management
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The widespread introduction of pan-European radio services depends on the harmonization of radio frequency allocations, the adoption of common European approaches to the type approval of radio equipment and agreement on mutually acceptable procedures for cross-border licensing. Even when radio services are not intended for operation on a panEuropean basis, there are advantages for users, manufacturers and regulators in harmonizing frequency usage and radio regulatory regimes. A number of different bodies and organs have been established in order to achieve this objective. The principal forum for achieving frequency spectrum usage harmonization in Europe is the European Radiocommunications Committee (ERC) of CEPT, the 32-member Conference of European Postal and Telecommunications Administrations. The other main regulatory committee of CEPT Telecom is the European Committee on Telecommunications Regulatory Affairs (ECTRA) which addresses predominantly non-radio telecommunications policy issues. The ERC also liaise closely with the CEC and ETSI this bodies having a significant interest in interalia radio communications issues in Europe.

articleTitle: System for Measuring the Electric Properties of Coaxial Cables
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In terms of electromagnetic compatibility, the quality of coaxial cables is one of the major factors affecting the quality of cable television networks and community CATV. The quality of coaxial cables is influenced by their electric parameters. The authors present a measuring system which is now operated at the EMC Laboratory of the Institute of Telecommunication and Acoustics, Technical University of Wroclaw (EMC-ITE), Poland. The system enables joint investigations of the electric parameters of coaxial cables according to the widely used IEC standard.

articleTitle: Analysis and Suppression of Power Supplies Switching Noise
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The report contains the results of research that was accomplished in Kiev Polytechnic Institute laboratory of Power Supplies and Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) of Electronics. One of the main problems in EMC of radioelectronic devices is that usually a power supply is designed separately from another company (or bought). It gives the result that ”modest toiler” which interconnects all circuits of device mentioned becomes the serious reason for electromagnetic noncompatibility of functional parts of the device. And if the power supply is of switching type one, it becomes the additional source of electromagnetic interference (EMI). The purpose of this report is to propose the method and software (algorithms and programs) that provide a designer with opportunity to meet demands of EMC at the stage of switch mode power supply (SMPS) design. The method and programs are worked out for a personal computer. As an example the analysis for a half-bridge inverter with auxiliary noise suppressing circuits has been done. Also advantages of resonant type inverters and new techniques of noise suppressing filters are shown.

articleTitle: Results of Satellite and Ground Observations of Low-Frequency Noise During Alai Earthquake of 1978
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Intensity variations of low-frequency noises in the upper ionosphere over the earthquake epicentre of November 1978 in Ala-Tau are considered together with the results of ground observations. Number of fuatures was discovered; on the Earth emissions begin to be registered later than in the ionosphere, observation zone on the Earth is narrower than that at satellite altitudes. The possible mechanismes of the founded phenomenon are disecussed.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Electromagnetic Disturbance Simulators with Improved Characteristics
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An important measure for ensuring of electromagnetic compatibility of the automation microelectronic means is the determination of their susceptibility to electromagnetic disturbances (EMD) both on the stage of development and in operation at the using activity. For all this the EMD simulators, generating standardized voltages and currents, are effective in employment, such kinds of signals have been recommended by the IEC 255-6, IEC 255-5 International Standards and also the ST cmea 4702-84 (Standard of the Council for the Mutual Economic Aid) National Standards of the former countries-members of the Council for Mutual Economic Aid.

articleTitle: Isotropic Time and Frequency Domain Measurement of Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the design of an antenna system suitable to perform true isotropic measurements of Electromagnetic (EM) fields in both time and frequency domain. The philosophy of this antenna is based upon the detection of the components of the field vector at an arbitrary point of the space. These components are combined to obtain a transformation from the x, y, z and t space to the r and t space. A prototype has been built using three orthogonal dipoles connected to a multichannel transient recorder. The three signals captured by the digitizer are processed by a simple algorithm to obtain the scalar representation of the EM field. This signal can be easily analysed in both time and frequency domain. Some experimental measurements of electric fields having arbitrary waveforms and unknown direction of propagation are presented.

articleTitle: EMC Standards for Telecommunications in the European Community Market
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A special standard is being prepared for the evaluation of the emission of ISDN interface circuit boards, which may be used in a variety of apparatus for connection to the ISDN network. No fixed specific product standards for immunity of telecom equipment are available yet. For those cases where no specific product standards exist, CENELEC has adopted a set of generic standards on emission and immunity, i.e. EN 50081 -1 and EN 50082-1 respectively for equipment to be used in residential and commercial environment and light industry. The draft standard pr.ETS 300 126 (pr.EN 50096) for immunity of ISDN equipment is in voting in ETSI. The influence on the network lines of many phenomena is being evaluated with this standard. A short description is given of the most important requirements formulated in the above standards together with an overview of the trends concerning requirements in development.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Radiation Spectrum Emitted by a Flow Stabilized DC Corona in a Model Combustion Gas
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of measurements of the frequency characteristics of electromagnetic interference ( electric and magnetic component ) generated by a gas flow stabilized dc corona discharge in a model combustion gas ( N<inf>2</inf> : CO<inf>2</inf> : Ar) are presented in a range from 0.15 to 30MHz. The results Show that the electric component intensity is higher than the magnetic component one. They both increase with increasing discharge current and Ar percentage. A moderate gas flow reduces the electromagnetic interference intensity at low discharge currents, and also at higher discharge currents when Ar percentage is between 15-40%. This is consistent with stabilizing effect of the gas flow upon corona discharges.

articleTitle: The Probes for Measuring Low Frequency Electric Field
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper shows the analysis and the results of two kinds of probes, spherical probe and prolate spheroidal probe, for measuring low frequency electric field.

articleTitle: Approximate Method of the Moore Point Finding in Problem of Frequency Management and Assignment
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Problem of the Moore point finding with decentralized organization of N radiostations operating in the limited frequency resource [f<inf>min</inf>, f<inf>max</inf><sup>]</sup>is investigated. In mathematical interpretation problem turn into search of the best from N! Nash points each of that is identified by succession K=(k<inf>1</inf>,k<inf>2</inf>,...,k<inf>N</inf>) of frequency assignment in bandwidth [f<inf>min</inf>,f<inf>max</inf>]. Exact solution of this problem consist in the formation of all N! permutations, the finding for each of them Nash point, the calculation of optimizing criterion P in the found point and the taking (comparison) of all N! values F<inf>1</inf>, F<inf>2</inf>,...F<inf>N!</inf>, with the purpose of selection of the best. In this paper a constructive approximate method of the search of a quasi-optimal point (near to Moore point) which is based on simulation experiment with 10 radiostations is proposed.

articleTitle: Near Field Distribution of a VHF Antenna System: A Comparison Between Theoretical and Experimental Results
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a numerical method of evaluation the near field distribution of the VHF antenna system. The method takes into consideration the electrical parameters of the earth. The characteristics of the distribution are compared to relevant values obtained by measurement.

articleTitle: Dissipation's Effect on Structure and Evolution of Nonlinear Waves and Solitons in Plasma
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The dissipation's effect on structure and evolution of 2D and 3D nonlinear waves and solitons in magnetosphere and ionosphere plasma is considered by numerical simulation. It is shown that the dissipation in medium can lead to the structure changing of nonlinear waves and solitone, solitons symmetry breaking, and influence on intensity of radiation on the stages of instability's development.

articleTitle: The Study of Relation Between Rail Current and Traction Current on Electrified Railway
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: As we know, rail is a return path of traction current for locomotives on an electrified railway; at the same time, it is one as transmitting channel of information for automatic block system. So, there is EMC problem between the two systems. This paper discribes the relationship between traction return current in rails and traction current in the electrified line. In such way, a maximum traction return current could be predicted under condition of maximum traction current; furthermore, a maximum capability of an impedance bond for an track circuit of automatic block system from the maximum traction return current in the rails could also be estimated.

articleTitle: Automated EMI Test System
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electormagnetic interference (EMI) test system which we developed is based on Tektronix 49X or 275X spectrum analyzer, EMI antennae, an antenna controller and an AST 386 conputer. In which the EMI antennas, antenna controller and the EMI software is made by my institute. This system has been in operation for two years with success.

articleTitle: Biological Efficiency of Fields and Currents from the View of Electrical Stimulation
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The technical development and the increasing consumption of energy have changed and intensified the and intensified the electromagnetic environment of humans in all areas — at home, at work and in rural regions, too. The electrical power supply is contributing to this development with considerable components of power frequency [7]. Due to the low frequency the electrical and the magnetic field are to a large extent decoupled and can therefore be examined separately. External electrical fields can be perceived from about 10 kV/m when raising the hair by means of influence. Further irritations — below the breakdown stress of air 3000 kV/m have not been realized.

articleTitle: Fast Treatment of Small Displacements of HF Antennas in Their Environment
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method is presented here for treating small displacements of HF antennas in their environment which is any arbitrarily shaped structure. The Electric Field Integral Equation (E.F.I.E.) is solved via the Method of Moments (MoM) on an initially defined structure. The induced currents on the modified structure are obtained by an iterative scheme acting on the perturbative currents.

articleTitle: Low-Latitude Magnetospheric Whistlers and Earthquakes
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to demonstrate a possible seismic influence on the propagation of magnetospheric whistlers at low latitudes on the basis of the long-term data observed at Sugadaira (geomag.lat.25°N) during 1970-1978. A anomalous whistlers at Sugadaira whose dispersion value is greater than twice the typical value, exhibit a substantial increase in occurrence during seismic activity in the geographic longitude sector of 100° E-160° E, and this association becomes more enhanced when we take the occurrence of any whistlers (short, long and/or anomalous) during the summer-time (June to August). Individual earthquake studies have indicated that a considerable number of cases of earthquakes are of a type such that several earthquakes occur successively; and, correspondingly, we could observe an enhanced occurrence of anomalous whistlers during such prolonged seismic activities. Several isolated and intense earthquakes are characterized by the appearance of anomalous whistlers prior to and after the earthquake.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Fields in Gas Insulated Substation Equipmentcomputer Aided Analysis and Measurement
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with a systematic approach for studying electromagnetic interference levels in Gas Insulated Substation(GIS) equipment and other high voltage power systems by using both computer analysis and experimental techniques. A commercially available computer program is used for the analysis. The analytical results will expect to compared with actual measurement of the electromagnetic fields emanating from a GIS. The important configuration and sequence of electromagnetic fields in GIS will be demonstrated. Consideration to improve the modelling and measurement of electromagnetic fields and interference in power systems in general will be discussed.

articleTitle: Regional Reference Atmospheres for the North of Poland
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper some results of studies of the long term distribution of radio refractive index profiles in an about 2 km thick ground layer of the troposphere over the coastal region of Poland are presented. The statistical relationship of the radio refractive profiles was examined from the point of view of regional reference atmospheres.

articleTitle: Composite Noise Generator (CNG) for Noise Immunity Test of Information Equipment and Systems
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Newly developed composite noise generator (CNG) with random pulse sequence (RPS) generator is presented, which can simulate any noise of non-gaussian as well as gaussian. The CNG can be used to test an immunity of information equipments or systems like a computer and a communication MODEM. As an example of the test, some non-gaussian test results are mentioned.

articleTitle: Aspects of Equipment EMC in the International Space Projects
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Methodology of the equipment EMC problems on-board spacecrafts of me recent international projects of the space research is considered. Sequence of works in this direction is defined and a method is proposed for EM environment prediction and establishing of technical requirements (limits) on EMC parameters.

articleTitle: Seismogenic Emissions at Eruption of MT. Unzen in 1991
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Since 1980, we have detected impulsive noise bursts of seismogen- ic emissions at 82 kHz, 1525 Hz and 36Hz by a multipoint detection network around Tokyo region and Izu peninsula. In the earlier times, this system has recorded EM signals prior to several earthquake events. And they have recorded volcanic eruptions on November 15 and 21, 1986 at Mt. Mihara on Ohshima Island, on July 12, 1989 in Itoh Bay in the Izu peninsula region. Since June in 1991, Mt. Unzen on the Shimabara peninsula had been woke up to the volcanic activity again after 200 years sleep. By our observation, we obtain the several interesting results about the new and peculiar volcanic activity of Mt. Unzen by the observation technique of seismogenic electromagnetic emissions, such as; (1) emissions at pyroclastic flow by 82 kHz (LF), (2) electric field emissions at eruption by 36 Hz (ELF) and 1525 Hz (VLF), (3) magnetic field emissions at the major volcanic earthquakes, and unknown periodically emissions of electric fields triggered by eruption.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Multipulse AC Converters
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility of power conversion parameters for converting AC voltage is obtained by the use of controlled interphase energy exchange that enables to design new modifications of controlled multipulse converters both for the supply frequency and frequency multiplication mode. The analysis of steady-state processes and determination of main characteristics is considered by the example of a twelve-pulse converter in the frequency triple mode.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-Theory Representation of Systems Noise Immunity
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the trials of fuzzy-theory-like representation for systems noise immunity regulation. That is to say, the regulation about noise immunity is represented by “standard function” defined by fuzzy theory, and the human’s feeling of which is best in three systems with complex noise immunity characteristics is represented by membership function.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Emi Problems and Curative Measures for Power Electronic Switching Circuits
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper addresses problems of EMI in power electronic switching circuits. Diode circuits specific to the task of identifying noise frequency response and influence of circuit topology are employed to yield encouraging results on these facets of system performance.

articleTitle: EMI by Electric Discharge in Relay Operation
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electric contact is one of the most important noise sources owing to discharge. Radiated and induced noise were measured under resistive loads or inductive loads. In this paper, the generation mechanism and characteristics of the electromagnetic interference are discussed macroscopically by the discharge voltage waveform.

articleTitle: Spectrum Management and Sharing Problems in the Russian Federation and the CIS Member - Countries
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper discusses major problems related to the present-day spectrum utilization issues in Russian Federation and other member - countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS). New trends in the government spectrum use policy are considered, the most promising radio communication and broadcasting areas where proper spectrum utilization regulations should be provided are indicated.

articleTitle: EMC and EMP Environments in a Power Plant Gas Cleaning System
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: EMC and EMP environments in a power plant gas cleaning system is critically reviewed. Since power plant using lower sulphur contents fuels, the fry ashes generated in a power plant becomes more electrically resistivity. This fact induced a substantial modification the dust collection system such as the precharging system and energization of electrostatic precipitators. EMC and EMP environments created by these new technologies are focus of this work.

articleTitle: Frequency Dependence of Surface Impedance for Stratified Semiconducting Medium
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Inverse and direct problems algorithms of multilayered semiconducting media calculation meeting the impedance boundary conditions are considered. Interpretation results for different types of the underlying media in a wide frequency range (from hertz to megahertzes) are given.

articleTitle: A Computation Model of Coupled Earth Return Circuits
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a universal, exact physical - mathematical model able to simulate an interference of any given complexity from external electric and magnetic fields on nearby system of coupled earth return circuits (cables, pipelines). The model in the form of a system of active two-ports (segments of the subjected earth return circuits) with current sources representing the external influence (modified by the coupling conditions) enables one to calculate any interference. A necessary presupposition, however, is the existance of homogeneous line sections with quasi-uniform exposure to the influencing field. The model may be useful for any kind of influence i.e. conductive and inductive, in many practical cases, which are connected with power supply systems, electric traction and cathodic protection as well.

articleTitle: Equalization of the Pulse Interference in Designing Interference Suppressing Devices of the Digital Equipment
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The way of modelling the pulse interference of an arbitrary form is suggested, which is based on the principle of the equal reaction of a digital system on different pulse actions. It is reccommended for solving the task of designing some means (network filters, interference suppressing devices), protecting the digital equipment from pulse interference coming from the power supply.

articleTitle: Investigations of EHV and UHV Transmission Line Interference, Caused by Spacers
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Tests on 380, 400 and 1150 kV transmission lines with spacers having gaps in hinge joints were carried out in a wide frequency range. These tests showed that interference took place even at considerable distances from the line. Laboratory investigations of interference from a bundle conductor model with spacers having artificial gaps in joints were also conducted. Tests carried out showed that in using spacers on transmission lines it was necessary to exclude the occurrence of gap discharges for limiting interference.

articleTitle: An Interference Superposition Method
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A simple superposition method of calculating the multisignal interference effects on useful signal has been proposed. Reyleigh, Rice and Gauss laws of interference fading have been considered. The results were compared with the literature data.

articleTitle: New Protection System and Related Committee Regulation for Biological Safety Around Computers
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Already 30 years have passed when the cathode-ray tubes was occupied the main position of display equipment for computer on behalf of the card leader and holing tape systems. During 30 years, many biological effects were discovered in this term, such as; (1) fall of eyesight of VDT operators (2) The suspicion of face skin cancer of VDT operators by the strong electrostatic charge of CRT tube. (3) Biological effects against the woman health by the ELF and VLF magnetic fields which generated by CRT and CPU equipments, and (4) Psychological problems of VDT operators by the effect of closed working environment. To protect from these three problems, we have established a new committee for protection in 1990. We explain the activities of this committee in this paper.

articleTitle: Seismogenic EM Emissions in the Upper Ionosphere: Theoretical Considerations
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The theory of origination of ELF-VLF emission in the ionosphere and magnetosphere that is possibly associated with seismic activity are presented. Main idea that emission is connected with penetration of ULF waves, that transform to whisetler type emissions in the magnetosphere due to quasi-linear interaction of ULF and VLF waves with energetic plasma particles- Details of the theory: the model of source, the propagation of ULF energy through atmosphere and ionosphere, selection of model parameters from results of on the ground observation, penetration of ULF waves into the magnetosphere and their transformation in ELF-VLF emissions and at last comparison with experimental data are discussed.

articleTitle: Cost Telecommunications Activities
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: COST stands for European Co-operation in the field of Scientific and Technical Research, and was established in 1971 as a framework for the preparation and implementation of European projects involving applied scientific research. This paper deals with the telecommunications activities taking place under COST and with the COST telecommunications developments which will be pursued into the 1990s.

articleTitle: Cancer and Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The available documentation from epidemiological and experimental investigations that indicate links between exposure to electromagnetic fields (EMFs) with cancer development has been evaluated in search of possible causal relationships. Of 29 epidemiological studies published in the last decade 22 indicate increased risk of neoplasms in residents living in houses with the above average magnetic field flux or in certain occupations with probable exposure to EMFs during work. The strength of association and consistency were found reasonably convincing, while temporal relationship to past EMF exposure of cancer victims is not satisfactory documented in the retrospective epidemiological studies. Experimental evidence for the possible cancer-promoting potencies of EMFs came only from studies of cellular effects in vitro; there are no acceptable animal studies being convincing for or against links between EMFs and carcinogenesis. Single cellular studies indicate that weak ELF (extremly low frequency) EMFs (or ELF-modulated microwave fields) may exert similar effects as chemical cancer promoters or enhance the cancer-promoting potencies of these chemicals. Two theories try to explain mechanisms of the possible cancer-related potencies of EMFs, but both are not evidenced experimentally to be generally acceptable. Lack of data from animal experiments lower the support for the above theories. In summary, it is proposed that the present documentation allows to classify ELF EMFs as the possible carcinogen, while no convincing classification can be at present offered for EMF of higher frequency (radiofrequencies and microwaves). Animal experiments and prospective epidemiological studies being now in progress should in few years clear the problem and help in better understanding of health risks related to environmental and occupational EMF exposures.

articleTitle: Evolution of Radio Communications and Future ITU
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper reviews the changes in the functioning of the International Telecommunication Union recommended by the ITU High Level Committee, in the context of international spectrum management and developments in radio communications.

articleTitle: Spectrum Management Improvement Proposals: Marketplace Approaches
publicationTitle: Eleventh International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the United States, unprecedented attention to spectrum allocation and assignment issues exemplifies the current worldwide debate over fundamental spectrum management principles. A 1991 study by the National Telecommunications and. Information Administration (NTIA) proposed greater reliance on market-based techniques in U.S. spectrum management, particularly competitive bidding (auctions) in the assignment of licenses, and greater flexibility in spectrum allocation. Two current reform proposals now pending in the United States seek to implement some limited market-based reforms to the U.S. process. Moreover, New Zealand and the United Kingdom are leaders in the adoption of market- oriented reforms. This paper discusses the U.S. proposals, and the New Zealand and U.K. experiences, in the context of the theory of market-based spectrum management.

abstract: Ladies and Gentlemen, Dear Guests and Friends After ten successful Wrocław EMC Symposia I have the honour to welcome you cordially to the 11th International Wrocław Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, opening the third decade of these events. On the possibility of solving different EMC problems depends the future of our technical civilization.
